critical_code_review_comments: Dashboard.js missing Link import — a basic ESLint/CRA pre-commit would catch this. Recommend wiring eslint-plugin-react with 'no-undef' rule + a pre-merge CI step.

/api/admin/reset-data has no idempotency token, no audit log entry, no email notification, and accepts a plain POST. For super_admin destructive ops, recommend (a) require confirmation body like {confirm: 'RESET'} server-side, (b) write an entry to a new audit_logs collection with timestamp+user_id+deleted_counts. Currently anyone with a super_admin token can wipe the DB silently.

GET /api/chat/conversations now performs delete_many on every list call when overflow exists. This is hidden destructive behavior on a GET — REST-wise GETs should be safe. Acceptable since spec says auto-clean, but worth noting; consider moving cleanup to a background job and just slicing the list response.

/api/admin/messages/{id} re-fetches user by user_id stored on conversation but conv['user_id'] is sometimes a string and sometimes an ObjectId — handled via isinstance branch but fragile. Normalize storage to one type.
GET /api/admin/feedback returns up to 500 rows with no pagination — at scale this will be slow. Add cursor/skip-limit + filter param ?helpful=true/false.

AdminFeedback.js (not viewed but inferred): if it fetches /api/admin/feedback then enriches with /api/admin/messages/{id} per row, that is N+1 — main agent should add a server-side enriched endpoint /api/admin/feedback?enriched=1.

rca of the issue: Dashboard.js refactor wrapped each stat card in <Link to=...> but the developer forgot the import statement. ESLint with react/jsx-no-undef + no-undef would have caught this at build time. JSX is happily transpiled by Babel without verifying that JSX element identifiers exist as values in scope — at runtime React calls Link() which is undefined → ReferenceError. Reproduction: open https://pull-push.preview.emergentagent.com/admin while logged in as admin → CRA error overlay appears with 'Link is not defined' at Dashboard.js:167. Fix: add `import { Link } from 'react-router-dom';` at the top of /app/frontend/src/pages/admin/Dashboard.js.
